viewer_sees: Two gunners crouch behind a Lewis gun at the left of a wheat paddock, aimed at one lone emu that stands calmly at the right; the emu tilts its head, then turns and strides away unhurried
A farmer stands in a dry wheat paddock, a fistful of thin withered ears in his hand, looking over cracked red earth and a sagging fence
Veterans in old khaki tunics stand on a raw block of poor sandy land with a surveyor's peg, a tent and a half-built shed, looking over scrub that is not yet cleared
Bags of unsold wheat stacked high at a railway siding under a tarpaulin, a farmer slumped on a sack; far along the line, the first emus appear at the edge of the paddock
CROWD-AS-TEXTURE — a broad river of emus pours through a gap in a fence line across the wheat, dust rising, a farmer small at the right edge watching
On a rough kitchen table a worn khaki army tunic with faded medal ribbons lies beside a slouch hat and a small brown photograph of a Lewis gun crew
Three farmers in dusty work clothes, hats in their hands, walk into the minister's office toward Pearce's broad desk
Pearce at his desk ticks off three conditions on three raised fingers, one after another, while the farmers across the desk nod
An army truck pulls up on a dirt road at Campion; Major Meredith steps down and two gunners lift two Lewis guns and crates of ammunition from the tray
Meredith lowers his binoculars; far across the paddock a line of about fifty emus stands at the horizon, small and out of range, while the gunners wait beside the gun
Farmers on foot and on horseback spread out across the paddock to drive the emus toward the gun; the emus split into small groups that run off in every direction
At the dam, Meredith and the gunners wait behind the Lewis gun as a wide wall of emus walks steadily toward them; the gun clacks and jams, the gunner works the handle, the flock keeps coming
A truck with a Lewis gun on its tray bounces across the paddock after a pair of emus that run easily ahead of it, the gunner clinging to the gun
LEDGER/ACCUMULATION — a heap of spent brass cartridge cases and empty ammunition crates grows beside the gun, a gunner tipping out one more tray
A gunner with a small notebook and a farmer argue at the fence over how many emus fell, the gunner showing his tally, the farmer sweeping an arm across the paddock
Meredith, dusty and level-faced, stands beside the truck while a gunner sits on the tray with his hat knocked to one side; behind them an emu strolls past the fence
In the House of Representatives, one member leans over his bench with a grin and a raised hand while the benches around him laugh
The army truck with the gunners drives away along the dirt road at the left while, at the right, the emus go on grazing in the wheat
The truck rolls back along the road, the gunners climb down and set the Lewis gun on its bipod at the verge; across the paddock emus break into small groups
Meredith unfolds a telegram beside the truck and reads it; the gunners begin loading the Lewis gun back onto the tray as emus graze beyond the fence
Meredith at a field table by lamplight writes his report, a neat row of ten brass cartridges and one grey emu feather beside the page
EMPTY AFTERMATH — grey-brown emu feathers drift over an empty wheat paddock at dusk, the fence line and one dead white gum quiet in the low light
At an archive desk under a lamp, a scholar's hands in a tweed sleeve circle one figure on a yellowed typed report with a pencil and shake their head slowly
Meredith stands on the dam bank at dusk as a long disciplined column of emus walks past him in single file like a division on parade, one turning its head to look at him
An empty dirt road at Campion with no truck on it and farmers waiting at the roadside; then at a government counter a clerk shakes his head and slides their written request back across to them
A clerk at a timber counter stamps a claim slip and slides a few coins across to a farmer, who pockets them and nods
LEDGER/ACCUMULATION — stamped claim slips pile up on the clerk's counter faster than he can file them, the heap spilling over the edge while the line of farmers outside reaches out the door
One emu stands tall on a red rise in the dawn light, the army truck small and far on the road below, leaving; the emu watches it go and lowers its head to graze
A farmer leans on a fence reading a newspaper with a dry nod; behind him the wheat stands tall and untouched, one emu far out at the edge of the paddock
MACRO OBJECT — along a weathered fence rail in warm evening light lie one grey emu feather, a short row of brass cartridges and a single stamped claim slip; a lone emu wanders the wheat beyond
End card: poster of the whole story with the title, the major and the emu, and the SUBSCRIBE button
